title: 1956 AHSME Problem 45
statement: A wheel with a rubber tire has an outside diameter of \(25\) in. When the radius has been decreased a quarter of an inch, the number of revolutions in one mile will:

solutions.text:
The original radius is \(12.5\) inches and the new radius is \(12.25\) inches. For a fixed distance, the number of revolutions varies inversely with radius, so the relative increase is \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{12.5}{12.25}-1 &=\frac{50}{49}-1\\ &=\frac1{49}\\ &\approx2.04\%. \end{aligned} \] This is about \(2\%.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: For a fixed distance, the revolution count is inversely proportional to the wheel’s radius
Compare the original radius \(12.5\) with the new radius \(12.25\)
